subject: SLA template: availability & latency carve-out proposal and monthly credit framing
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Meyers <sarah.meyers@greenline.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template: availability & latency carve-out proposal and monthly credit framing

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. As promised, I attached a draft SLA that aligns with our hosted inference offering and the commercial terms we discussed with your team. This note pulls out two items we expect will need explicit alignment from procurement/legal:

- Availability baseline: we propose a 99.9% monthly availability baseline for the hosted API in the US region, with a separate 99.8% baseline for EU (regional routing differences).
- Monthly service credits: in the event of a breach, credits are tiered by monthly availability bands (example matrix attached). Our starting point is 5% of monthly invoice for availability in [99.5% — 99.9%), 15% for [99.0% — 99.5%), and 50% for <99.0%.

Two carve-outs we want to flag up front so we can avoid surprises: scheduled maintenance windows (we propose a monthly maintenance allowance of up to 3 hours, announced with minimum 72-hour notice) and emergency regional routing changes for extreme outages (we limit aggregated emergency maintenance to 6 hours/month for force-majeure and provider-side infra incidents).

I attached the redline (SLA-proposal-redwood-v2.pdf) and a simple credit matrix spreadsheet. Could you confirm which points procurement wants tightened versus where Greenline needs more tolerance? If useful, happy to run a short call with your legal and our product ops to walk the carve-outs.

Thanks,
Connor
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA-proposal-redwood-v2.pdf (pdf), monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Sarah Meyers <sarah.meyers@greenline.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenline.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: availability & latency carve-out proposal and monthly credit framing

Connor —

Thanks for the draft and the clear note. A few initial clarifying questions from procurement/legal:

1) Can you explain the rationale for different baselines by region? Greenline needs a unified customer-facing SLA; having multiple baselines complicates internal reporting.
2) The credit tiers look acceptable in principle but procurement has two asks: a cap on total monthly credits (we typically see a 100% monthly cap) and a faster remediation window for high-severity incidents (we'd like 4-hour detection-to-response for Sev1).
3) Maintenance notice: 72 hours is OK, but can Redwood guarantee maintenance windows won't coincide with Greenline's scheduled daily peak (we operate heavy inference between 16:00-20:00 UTC)?

We can do a short call Friday if that works — please propose times.

Best,
Sarah
Sr. Procurement Manager
Greenline
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Meyers <sarah.meyers@greenline.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: availability & latency carve-out proposal and monthly credit framing

Sarah —

Appreciate the quick reading and good questions. Short answers up front:

1) Regional baselines: the split is driven by our current regional redundancy topology and routing guarantees. Technically we can offer a unified 99.9% baseline globally if Greenline takes our multi-region routing addendum (we'll pin the API to a primary region for billing/metrics). If Greenline needs a single SLA, we can collapse to 99.9% but would like an explicit clause that regional failover time may affect per-request latency during cross-region failover.

2) Credit cap: we are amenable to a monthly credit cap at 100% of monthly invoices. For Sev1 response windows, our standard is "acknowledge within 1 hour, mitigation plan in 4 hours"; we can commit to a 4-hour mitigation plan for Sev1 (we'll put the playbook in the appendix).

3) Maintenance: we cannot guarantee avoidance of all customer peak windows globally, but we can offer targeted blackout windows — if Greenline provides a list of daily/weekly peak windows per region we will commit to not schedule maintenance in those windows except for emergency maintenance (where we'll give as much notice as possible).

Suggested next step: call Friday 10:00–10:30 PST to align on the unified baseline vs regional split and the credit cap. If that works for you I'll send a calendar invite and bring our product reliability lead (Priyom) and contract manager (Laura).

Regards,
Connor
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 6 Jun 2025 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommended carve language and credit tweak for Greenline call

Connor / Laura / Marissa —

Quick internal note ahead of the call: a few product/legal suggestions to streamline negotiation

- Flatten to a single baseline of 99.9% globally but add an explicit "regional failover latency" paragraph — proposed language: "In the event of cross-region failover, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to restore request latency to baseline within 120 minutes; during this period, availability counts against the applicable monthly baseline."
- Cap on credits: accept 100% monthly invoice cap but add a quarterly reconciliation clause that allows Redwood to present remediation evidence to limit payouts for incidents caused by customer traffic spikes outside agreed thresholds.
- Maintenance: propose a two-tier maintenance notice: 72 hours for standard maintenance; 6 hours for emergency infrastructure patches with a hard cap of 6 emergency hours per rolling 30-day window.
- Latency SLO: avoid absolute per-request latency commitments in the SLA; instead, include a P95/P99 observability commitment and an acknowledgement timeline for Sev2/Sev1 incidents.

I'll be on the call to explain the operational realities.

— Priyom
Senior Product Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Meyers <sarah.meyers@greenline.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Jun 2025 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: availability & latency carve-out proposal and monthly credit framing

Sarah —

Thanks for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, Redwood can move forward with the following compromises in the next redline:

- Single global baseline at 99.9% (Greenline to confirm whether multi-region routing option is desired in writing).
- Monthly credit tiers retained as proposed, with a 100% monthly invoice cap.
- Added appendix language on cross-region failover latency (we'll use Priyom's suggested paragraph).
- Commitment to a 4-hour mitigation plan for Sev1 incidents with 1-hour acknowledgement SLA.
- Maintenance schedule: 72-hr notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance limited to 6 hours/30-day window.

I've asked our contracts team to produce a redline that reflects these points and will circulate a DocuSign link once Greenline confirms the multi-region option and the blackout windows you mentioned.

Next steps for Greenline: 1) confirm if you want the multi-region routing addendum; 2) provide list of daily peak windows by region (UTC offsets) so we can lock blackout periods; 3) confirm procurement is comfortable with the 100% monthly cap.

I'll follow up early Monday with the redlined PDF and a DocuSign link for quick execution if all looks good.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments mentioned in thread: SLA-proposal-redwood-v2.pdf, monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx
